body_text:
Absolute convergence implies convergence: if $\sum|a_n|<\infty$,
then $\sum a_n$ converges. For absolutely convergent series, every
rearrangement has the same sum. A conditionally convergent real
series behaves differently: its terms can be rearranged to
converge to any prescribed real value or to diverge.
